discovery: Actually returned T-pool identity explicitly assigned by control; research does not assert backend selection or qualification.

source_groups.origin: Company-controlled website; four pages share claim origin.
Original papers by overlapping commercial/academic collaborators. Publisher hosting is not independent replication; company-associated authors and commercial interests limit independence.

claims: Company describes oncology target discovery followed by biological validation and partnering of preclinical programs.
limits: Target/package counts and safety/efficacy claims were not independently validated; avoid repeating industry-wide failure statistics as company evidence.

claims: Company describes integrating dependency/biomarker evidence, then testing in disease-relevant and patient-derived systems with normal comparators before packaging assets.
limits: Workflow description alone does not establish successful validation, a therapeutic window, or clinical translation.

claims: Company describes small-molecule multiple-myeloma work with SARomics, AML target work with Sprint Bioscience, and AML/MM peptide exploration with AffinityAI.
Several additional indication entries describe targets awaiting further validation.
limits: Do not turn target candidates, planned validation or collaboration descriptions into nominated drugs or completed studies.
The page does not establish ownership of the DCPS program studied in the papers below.

claims: Company names Julian Walfridsson and Mikael Altun as scientific founders; lists Walfridsson as CSO/founder, Thomas Binzer as CEO, and Andreas Hoglund as head of biology; describes preclinical partnering/licensing/sale.
limits: Do not infer Binzer is a founder, equate institutional affiliation with asset rights, or infer current founding-team composition/tenure.

claims: Original Leukemia paper reports investigating low-FHIT AML vulnerability to DCPS inhibition, including cell-line drug perturbation and FHIT manipulation; Walfridsson is listed with a NeoTargets affiliation.
limits: Main text inspected; supplementary experiments/data were not separately retrieved or reproduced.
Experimental activity in these models is not proof of patient benefit or NeoTargets ownership of an asset.
Paper and 2026 follow-up share research origin; do not count them as independent replications.

claims: Follow-up reports ex vivo primary-AML testing of RG3039 and biomarker analysis; hydroxyurea pretreatment confounds FHIT prediction, while IDH2 is explored as a proxy.

Contributions attribute supervision/funding acquisition to Walfridsson and Hoglund; Hoglund also has conceptualization, formal-analysis and data-access roles. Experimental validation is attributed to other named collaborators.
limits: Patient-derived samples are not a prospective treatment trial. MDS functional validation is still needed; some primary data require permission/request.
Paper discloses NeoTargets/Sprint employment and shareholdings. Specific contributions do not establish sole invention or all company claims.
Underlying raw data and supplementary material were not reproduced; current drug rights, development status and efficacy remain unresolved.
